segments.text: This tutorial introduces the basics of Docker containers.
A container packages an application together with its dependencies.
Unlike a virtual machine a container shares the host operating system kernel.
That makes containers lightweight and fast to start.
You describe an image using a text file called a Dockerfile.
The FROM instruction sets the base image to build on.
The COPY instruction adds your source code into the image.
The RUN instruction executes commands during the build.
You build an image with the docker build command.
You start a container with the docker run command.
Map a container port to the host using the dash p flag.
Persist data outside the container by mounting a volume.
Push your image to a registry so others can pull and run it.
Keep images small by using a minimal base and multi stage builds.
That covers the essential Docker workflow.
